transcript.text: Every so often when I put the washing machine on the whole kitchen power goes off and I have to go to the fuse box and flick the switch back up. It doesn't happen every time. Indesit, IWE 7 something.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. This is most likely an intermittent electrical earth fault, not normal behaviour. Do not use the washing machine again until it has been checked by a qualified appliance engineer; repeatedly resetting the breaker is unsafe. If it trips later in a wash, the heater element is the usual suspect; if it trips immediately, the mains lead/plug, mains filter, wiring, pump or motor become more likely. With the machine switched off and unplugged, you can only safely look for obvious damage to the plug and lead, or signs of water around the machine—do not remove panels. Does it trip as soon as the machine is switched on/started, or only later in the wash (often around 10–30 minutes, when it begins heating)?

Thanks, I've been keeping notes, so I can answer that. It only trips a few minutes into the wash, never as soon as I switch it on. It has only happened on the 40 and 60 degree washes. It has never happened on a cold wash, the quick 30, or rinse and spin. Over the last month it's been roughly 1 wash in 4.

I should admit I have been resetting it each time and carrying on, as I didn't realise that was a problem. I haven't smelled any burning or seen any sparks, and the plug looks fine and isn't warm.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. That pattern points very strongly to the heater element developing an intermittent earth fault: it occurs on the hotter programmes, a few minutes into the cycle when heating begins, and not on cold/rinse-and-spin cycles. The less likely alternatives are the heater wiring or its control circuit. Please leave the machine unplugged and arrange a qualified appliance engineer; they can insulation-test the heater and associated wiring with the appliance isolated, which will confirm it. Do not run further test washes or reset the breaker to continue a cycle.

candidates: Heater element insulation fault to earth (high)
Damaged mains lead, plug, interference filter or internal wiring (medium)
Drain pump or motor electrical fault (low)
